evals.prompt: Build the KPI row for the dashboard home: total users, revenue, active projects and conversion rate. Make total users the standout card and give each card a different colour so the row doesn't look flat.
evals.expected_output: A responsive grid of four MetricCard instances — one hero variant spanning extra columns with an explicit widest-breakpoint reset, the rest icon/default variants with different categorical icon-color tokens — wrapped in .stagger-children.
assertions: Imports MetricCard from ~/components/shared/MetricCard.vue and does not hand-roll a stat card
Exactly one card uses variant="hero" and it passes a column span plus a widest-breakpoint reset (e.g. sm:col-span-2 xl:col-span-1)
icon-color values differ across the row (chart-1, chart-2, chart-3, chart-4)
The grid wrapper carries the .stagger-children class
Values are passed as formatted display strings, with no separate count-up wiring

evals.prompt: For the SaaS dashboard I need MRR as a sparkline over the last 12 months and a progress card for the quarterly revenue quota ($340k of $500k).
evals.expected_output: One sparkline MetricCard with 7–14 realistic sparkData points and one progress card driven by progress.current/progress.max, both using the pre-built component.
assertions: sparkData has 7–14 points with natural variation, not a trivially increasing sequence
The progress card passes progress: { current, max } rather than a custom bar
No inline SVG or custom progress markup is hand-rolled
Both cards are MetricCard instances from ~/components/shared/MetricCard.vue

evals.prompt: The dashboard KPIs load from the API and take a moment. While loading, the row currently jumps because the cards pop in with dashes; make it feel stable.
evals.expected_output: The same MetricCard grid with the loading prop set while data is pending, so skeletons hold the layout instead of placeholder values; formatted values appear when data resolves.
assertions: Passes :loading to MetricCard while the request is pending
Does not render placeholder text like '--' or 0 as the loading treatment
The grid keeps the same column classes so layout does not shift
Resolved values are formatted display strings
